newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG natgas storage expansion considered.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG natgas storage expansion considered.

text.p: The New York State Public Service Commission said Thursday it will hold hearings for public comment on the New York State Electric & Gas Corp's (NYSEG) application to construct two additional natural gas compressors and associated equipment to be used in conjunction with its Seneca Lake Gas Storage Project.

The two proposed 2,587-horsepower, natural gas-fueled, single-stage reciprocating compressors would be located wholly within NYSEG's existing compression station site in the Town of Reading, Schuyler County.

NYSEG states that the proposal would provide it the capability to offer high deliverability gas storage service to customers in interstate commerce with rates and services regulated by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

The company further states that no additional work would be required on the previously certified Seneca Lake Storage gas transmission lines and that there would be no increase in the maximum operating pressure of the pipeline. It indicates that it will seek no recovery of additional costs associated with the proposal from its ratepayers, the commission said.
